column2: Does she need to bring ID?
She said she would call that night.
Does she have to work today?
You had better not touch that wire.
No. Didn't need to says there was no necessity; the sentence adds that the speaker bought one anyway.
No. Won't work can mean that the printer refuses to function now, even after a restart.
I had to leave early yesterday.
Could have taken expresses a possibility about the past; the sentence says we do not know which train he took.
You had better save a copy.
You shouldn't touch the hot tray.
Tickets are free, so you don't have to pay.
I was not able to finish on time.
He had the opportunity to take the earlier train but did not; he chose to wait.
You must keep this medicine cool.
No. In this context may not can mean that perhaps she does not know the password; prohibition requires a different context.
It expresses an expectation that the bus has probably arrived by now, not advice about what it ought to have done.
You had better check the address.
May not expresses a prohibition on a sign: visitors are not permitted to enter.
She is supposed to arrive by nine.
We need to check the total.
She did not need to attend.
We were not allowed to enter that room yesterday.
They managed to find the missing file.
We will not have to move.
You ought not to ignore the warning.
The windows must be cleaned by the caretakers every week.
Could swim describes a general ability at ten; managed to swim to safety reports a successful action after the boat sank.
Should is advice; had better is more urgent here and warns of a likely consequence.
Must leave expresses a present or future requirement; must have left is a strong deduction about the past.
It is an expectation that the parcel will probably arrive tomorrow, not advice to the parcel.
Have is the main verb meaning possess; must have a passport is a requirement, not a perfect form.
No. Needn't have finished can refer to a completed action before a future deadline; Friday need not already have passed.
No. May be being repaired combines a modal, the continuous form and a passive; the repeated be-forms have different jobs.
I have got to leave now.
I will be able to travel next month.
The door needs to be painted.
Mustn't call means calling is forbidden; don't have to call means calling is optional.
You must submit the form before noon tomorrow.
I want to be able to play the piano.
Would you send me the timetable, please?
